subject: Socket fan-out & rate-path handoff — parallelism qualification and quota ask
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cho <sam@quantaretail.com>, Priya Desai <priya@quantaretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Socket fan-out & rate-path handoff — parallelism qualification and quota ask

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to align on traffic shape and the POC objectives. Quick recap + asks so we can move the quota discussion to a proposal: 

Summary of what we heard from QuantaRetail today:
- Workload: product recommendations + lightweight personalization scoring, mix of sync gRPC requests and long-lived streaming sessions for session-aware scoring.
- Traffic profile: ~120 TPS average across the day, spiky peaks up to ~700 TPS during promo windows (~3–5 minute bursts).
- Latency targets: p95 <= 180 ms for sync calls; tail for streaming checkpoints <= 350 ms.
- Concurrent sessions: 3,000 active user sessions with ~30% making concurrent scoring calls (~900 parallel streams), plus a separate batch of ~200 parallel ad-hoc sync requests at peaks.

Key qualification questions / asks from Redwood for a firm quota proposal:
1) Can you confirm whether the ~3,000 active sessions are long-lived WebSocket connections that need per-session KV cache affinity, or short-lived reconnects?
2) For the 900 parallel streams figure, what % are low-throughput keep-alives vs. actively streaming tokens? (helpful for prefix-KV cache sizing)
3) Are sync gRPC calls mTLS-authenticated and routed through a single public IP (we can optimize connection pooling) or via multiple egress IPs?

Proposed negotiation points (what we'll include in the rate-path proposal):
- Baseline concurrency reservation: 1,200 parallel server-side request slots (covers steady + steady-state burst handling)
- Staged burst window: allow 5-minute elastic bursts up to 800 extra parallel slots during promo windows (metered, with overage credits)
- Connection pooling guidance: recommend 150 keep-alive sockets per region for the app tier; will support both gRPC multiplexing and WebSocket fan-out.
- Rate limits: 1,000 TPS sustained per model endpoint; 5,000 TPS short-burst cap with gradual backpressure and per-customer fair-queueing.

Attachments: conn_profile.pdf (your connection diagram) — pulled into our engineering review.

Next steps I propose:
- Please answer the three qualification questions above by end of day Friday.
- Laura from our SRE team will run a quick mapping exercise once we receive the reconnect/stream ratio — should take ~1 business day.
- If confirmed, we’ll put a draft quota and price path in the redwood-ratecard-v2.xlsx and route for approvals.

If helpful we can schedule a short technical deep-dive with our infra team (30m) to walkthrough socket fan-out and graceful-degrade behavior under bursts.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Sam Cho <sam@quantaretail.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Socket fan-out & rate-path handoff — parallelism qualification and quota ask

Thanks Irene — useful recap. Quick answers inline: 

On Thu, Jul 11, 2029 at 09:12, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm whether the ~3,000 active sessions are long-lived WebSocket connections that need per-session KV cache affinity, or short-lived reconnects?

The sessions are long-lived WebSockets from client browsers to our edge tier. They stay open for the full shopping session (~20–40 minutes) with occasional reconnects on network changes (~<5% of sessions/hour). We would like Redwood to maintain KV affinity per session where practical (session id passed in metadata).

> 2) For the 900 parallel streams figure, what % are low-throughput keep-alives vs. actively streaming tokens?

Estimate: ~65% are keep-alives with infrequent token sends. ~35% are active during a shopping flow and will produce bursts of tokens for the recommendation pipeline (avg 4–12 tokens per active event).

> 3) Are sync gRPC calls mTLS-authenticated and routed through a single public IP (we can optimize connection pooling) or via multiple egress IPs?

Sync calls are mTLS and exit via a small NAT pool (3 public IPs) per region. We can consolidate to one egress IP if that helps connection reuse.

Procurement note: procurement will want to see the burst economics (how overage is billed). Can you include an example cost run for a 2-hour promo spike that sustains 5x baseline TPS?

Also: we’re happy to run the 2-week POC once we get the trial keys and baseline quota.

—Sam
Sam Cho
Head of Edge Engineering — QuantaRetail
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cho <sam@quantaretail.com>, Priya Desai <priya@quantaretail.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Socket fan-out & rate-path handoff — parallelism qualification and quota ask

Hi Sam / Priya — thanks for the rapid answers, that helps. A few notes from infra + a draft quota we’ll put in the workbook: 

Engineering clarifications based on your answers:
- Long-lived WebSockets with KV affinity: we’ll allocate sticky routing for session IDs and reserve dedicated KV cache lines for the active session set. That reduces token recomputation on reconnects.
- Keep-alive ratio: given 65% keep-alive, we will size the connection pool differently from the active token slots.

Draft quota proposal (subject to legal/pricing signoff):
- Reserved concurrency: 1,250 parallel request slots (covers sync + active streams).
- Socket pool reservation: 2,800 keep-alive sockets reserved (maps to your ~3,000 sessions with headroom).
- Burst window policy: tiered approach — automatic elastic window up to 800 extra parallel slots for 5 minutes; extended bursts beyond that will trigger queued requests with 30s timeout and optional fallback model.
- Rate limits: 1,200 TPS sustained per customer across endpoints; short-burst cap 6,000 TPS with progressive backpressure.
- Pricing model example (included in redwood-ratecard-v2.xlsx): we calculated a 2-hour 5x spike on an assumed baseline of 120 TPS — rough overage delta shows ~$4.8k incremental for that promo depending on caching ratio. We’ll include two scenarios (with and without prefix caching).

Next steps and handoff:
1) We’ll upload the full workbook (redwood-ratecard-v2.xlsx) with line-item math and an appendix showing how prefix-KV hit rate impacts cost.
2) Aditya will set up a short demo/POC runbook for your infra team that includes a test harness to simulate 5x spikes and show graceful-degrade behavior.
3) If QuantaRetail confirms egress consolidation to a single IP, Aditya can provide connection pooling knobs to reduce socket counts and improve reuse.

Irene will follow with the formal proposal. If you want the POC earlier we can spin up trial keys today pending procurement approval.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Laura / team — this looks reasonable and aligns with what procurement asked for. A couple of small items before we sign the POC paperwork: 

- Can you add a line in the workbook that explicitly models the case where caching hit-rate improves from 40% to 70% (we expect to tune this during the POC).
- For the short-burst cap, will Redwood expose metrics (per-minute TPS, queue length, dropped requests) to our monitoring? We need a way to tie behavior to our SLOs during the POC.

If those two items are included we’ll route the draft for procurement approval this afternoon and expect to complete the DocuSign sign-off by EOD Monday. We also confirm we can consolidate egress to a single IP — we’ll follow up with network ops on the change window.

Next steps per us: procurement requests the DocuSign link and an official POC SOW. If possible include a 30% credit buffer in the first invoice for the POC ramp (this can be applied as a one-time credit).

Thanks — Sam
